Surf trips from New England · scored & ranked · Aug 2026

The Family Wave Index

122 destination-plus-season trips scored on ten dimensions, ranked three ways: a family division (everyone scores, beginner floor), a solo/boys division (advanced crews, wave count first), and a strike division (don't book dates — watch the chart and fly when it's confirmed). Same trips, same scores; only the weights and the gate change. Wave pools are a toggle: off, they appear untiered as calibration rows; on, they compete — and in the family division a pool only counts when it's part of a resort.

How the score works

Each trip is a destination + season window, scored 0–10 on nine dimensions against written anchors; a division's composite is its weighted sum on a 0–100 scale. The family weighting puts swell certainty and the turnkey factor first and gates on a beginner floor; the solo/boys weighting — derived from a charger + charter-captain + defender persona panel — promotes crowds, quality, and advanced, demotes lodging and beginner, and gates on an advanced floor instead.

Provenance, honestly. Scores are structured expert priors from swell climatology and the surf-travel record as of early 2026 — an ordinal ranking tool, not measurements. A 3-point gap is meaningful; a 1-point gap is noise. Crowd scores decay fastest in real life; safety scores reflect early-2026 conditions — re-check advisories before booking. Full anchors and the v1→v7 changelog (incl. rejected proposals) live in METHODOLOGY.md; rerun score.py + gen_report.py to regenerate everything here.

The top ten — mixed-ability division

These ten pass the beginner floor (beginner score ≥ 6 (pools: on-site resort required)): the whole family gets real waves, not just the strongest surfer. The pattern is unmistakable: access-controlled, guide-driven operations win — boat-resort models and gated point-break setups buy the two things money usually can't: empty lineups and daily wave certainty. Experts-first trips (marked ✗ below) still appear in the full table with their scores intact.

Cloudbreak/Restaurants for the chargers, Swimming Pools for improvers, island-capped guest counts, legendary family weeks with kids' programs. As close as it gets to guaranteed world-class waves with a family wrapper. Booking: Named family weeks only (min age otherwise); 12–18mo.

79.8

The academy model at its peak: a performance surf school (video analysis, structured coaching, quiver included) wrapped in a boutique hotel whose pool overlooks the El Palmarcito point, with Sunzal-to-Punta-Roca in guided range. The most professionalized coaching product in the hemisphere — a property-level entrant the coastline row couldn't see, added v11. Booking: Hotel + academy; 3–6mo.

When to go where

The year splits cleanly in two: April–October belongs to the Southern Hemisphere swell machine, November–March to North Atlantic and North Pacific winter, with the Portugal/France shoulder peaking September–October. Gate-passing trips only.

Apr – Oct · southern season

The guarantee window

  1. Namotu / Tavarua island resorts 86.0 · Apr–Oct

Three ways to book it

The full-service boat resort

Namotu/Tavarua, Telos, Maldives, Las Flores. One booking buys guides, boats, kids' programs and the pool over the break. Highest floor, highest cost, longest flights. Book 9–12 months out — family weeks sell out first.

The gated point-break villa

Rancho Santana, Popoyo, El Zonte, Mizata. A house or small resort inside a surf community, a local guide with a panga or truck. Near-resort wave access at a third of the price, 6–7h door to door.

The easy strike

Rincón, Barbados, Azores, Canaries. Nonstop flights, book two weeks out when the seasonal forecast firms up. Lower guarantee, minimal commitment — the repeatable school-vacation play.

The top ten — mixed-ability division

These ten pass the beginner floor (beginner score ≥ 6 (pools: on-site resort required)): the whole family gets real waves, not just the strongest surfer. The pattern is unmistakable: access-controlled, guide-driven operations win — boat-resort models and gated point-break setups buy the two things money usually can't: empty lineups and daily wave certainty. Experts-first trips (marked ✗ below) still appear in the full table with their scores intact.

1

Surf Ranch (Lemoore)

91.6
USA (California)·Year-round·$$$$·min 2d·55–75°F · 3/2 typical (4/3 winter)·BOS→FAT ~9h + 1h drive

The best artificial wave on earth, run like a private club: your group alone, a wave count no ocean lineup allows, on-site cabins. Scarcity is the catch — strikeability 4 because you book it like a resort, not a swell. Booking: Private hire via broker/invite; long waits.

When to go where

The year splits cleanly in two: April–October belongs to the Southern Hemisphere swell machine, November–March to North Atlantic and North Pacific winter, with the Portugal/France shoulder peaking September–October. Gate-passing trips only.

Apr – Oct · southern season

The guarantee window

  1. Namotu / Tavarua island resorts 86.0 · Apr–Oct

Three ways to book it

The full-service boat resort

Namotu/Tavarua, Telos, Maldives, Las Flores. One booking buys guides, boats, kids' programs and the pool over the break. Highest floor, highest cost, longest flights. Book 9–12 months out — family weeks sell out first.

The gated point-break villa

Rancho Santana, Popoyo, El Zonte, Mizata. A house or small resort inside a surf community, a local guide with a panga or truck. Near-resort wave access at a third of the price, 6–7h door to door.

The easy strike

Rincón, Barbados, Azores, Canaries. Nonstop flights, book two weeks out when the seasonal forecast firms up. Lower guarantee, minimal commitment — the repeatable school-vacation play.

The top ten — charger division

The experts-first trips the family division flags ✗ — Salina Cruz, Mentawai, Nihi, P-Pass — are exactly what surfaces here.

Boys-mode caveats (from the panel's defender). The family-lens gaps the defender flagged were closed in v6 — the universe now includes the boys-first rows (Mentawai boat charter, a North Shore Oahu base, G-Land, Zicatela-proper, Nias, Krui). Two reading notes remain: Nihi Sumba's rank is partly a luxury artifact (you'd be paying $$$$ for an infinity pool this mode says you don't need), and Taghazout's turnkey 9 encodes a learner-camp industry an advanced crew uses less of. Cost and min-days filter harder than the weights here: the top of this division skews $$$$ and 10+ days — Salina Cruz ($$) and Chicama ($) are the value line.

All 122 trips — solo / boys trip weighting

Band = where the trip's rank lands when any one weight is perturbed ±25% — a tight band means the rank is robust. Crew = this division's gate (advanced score ≥ 7 and wave quality score ≥ 7). Filters below apply to this table only — the top-ten cards and calendar always show the model's unfiltered opinion. Rank numbers keep their gaps so you can see what a filter costs you.

When to go where

The year splits cleanly in two: April–October belongs to the Southern Hemisphere swell machine, November–March to North Atlantic and North Pacific winter, with the Portugal/France shoulder peaking September–October. Gate-passing trips only.

Apr – Oct · southern season

The guarantee window

  1. Namotu / Tavarua island resorts 87.9 · Apr–Oct
  2. Telo Islands (Resort Latitude Zero) 87.8 · Apr–Oct
  3. Mentawai boat charter 85.5 · Apr–Oct
  4. Las Flores + Punta Mango (boat resort) 85.5 · Apr–Sep
  5. Central/South atolls resort (Laamu, Six Senses area) 85.5 · Apr–Oct
  6. North Malé surf resort (Pasta Point/Sultans) 84.5 · Apr–Oct

Three ways to book it

The boat-and-boards program

Mentawai, Telos, Banyaks, Namotu. A charter or island camp where the program IS the trip: dawn call, boat to whichever reef is firing, repeat. Maximum waves per day money can buy; book 6–12 months out.

The guided strike camp

Salina Cruz, Las Flores, Kavieng. A guide with a truck or panga and gated access to sand-bottom points. Near-private lineups without charter prices.

The mileage basecamp

Chicama, Popoyo, Cabo Ledo, Puerto Escondido. Cheap, consistent, uncrowded — park the crew for 10 days, surf three sessions a day, spend the savings on the next trip.

No. 1 · 92.8

The top ten — charger division

Same trips, same scores — reweighted for a crew of advanced surfers with no beginners to protect: wave count and wave ceiling first, lodging demoted to "a bed near the break," and an advanced floor (advanced score ≥ 7 and wave quality score ≥ 7) replacing the beginner gate. The experts-first trips the family division flags ✗ — Salina Cruz, Mentawai, Nihi, P-Pass — are exactly what surfaces here.

1

Surf Ranch (Lemoore)

92.8
USA (California)·Year-round·$$$$·min 2d·55–75°F · 3/2 typical (4/3 winter)·BOS→FAT ~9h + 1h drive
Consistency10Crowds10Wave quality9Beginner7.5Advanced9Family safety9.5Turnkey10Lodging8Travel ease6.5Strike4

The best artificial wave on earth, run like a private club: your group alone, a wave count no ocean lineup allows, on-site cabins. Scarcity is the catch — strikeability 4 because you book it like a resort, not a swell. Booking: Private hire via broker/invite; long waits.

2

Namotu / Tavarua island resorts

87.9
Fiji·Apr–Oct·$$$$·min 8d·76–82°F · trunks (spring top Jul–Aug)·BOS→LAX→NAN ~19h + boat
Consistency9Crowds8.5Wave quality9.5Beginner6Advanced10Family safety9Turnkey10Lodging9.5Travel ease3Strike2

Cloudbreak/Restaurants for the chargers, Swimming Pools for improvers, island-capped guest counts, legendary family weeks with kids' programs. As close as it gets to guaranteed world-class waves with a family wrapper. Booking: Named family weeks only (min age otherwise); 12–18mo.

3

Telo Islands (Resort Latitude Zero)

87.8
Indonesia·Apr–Oct·$$$$·min 12d·82–85°F · trunks·BOS→SIN + charter ~30h
Consistency9.5Crowds9.5Wave quality9Beginner6.5Advanced9.5Family safety8Turnkey10Lodging9.5Travel ease1.5Strike1

Purpose-built family surf resort: ~20 breaks for a dozen guests, boat-guided by wave-of-the-tide, pool deck facing the surf, kids' programs. The archetype of 'everyone scores daily' — at expedition distance and price. Booking: Fixed 10–12nt charter rotations ex-SIN; 12mo+.

4

Waco Surf (Texas)

87.2
USA (Texas)·Year-round·$$·min 3d·50–88°F · seasonal: trunks (May–Sep) to 4/3 (winter)·BOS→DFW/AUS + 1.5h drive ~8-9h
Consistency10Crowds8.5Wave quality7.5Beginner10Advanced8Family safety9.5Turnkey9.5Lodging8Travel ease7Strike9.5

The flagship US pool: scheduled perfect waves, lifeguards, on-site casitas and a lazy river — a genuine resort, which is what qualifies it for the family division when pools are toggled on. Its score also remains the model's calibration diagnostic: it outscores every ocean trip. Booking: Book sessions online; private hire available.

5

Mentawai boat charter

85.5
Indonesia·Apr–Oct·$$$$·min 11d·82–85°F · trunks·BOS→PDG ~28h + liveaboard
Consistency10Crowds9Wave quality10Beginner3Advanced10Family safety5.5Turnkey9.5Lodging7Travel ease1.5Strike1

The boys-trip archetype the family lens excluded: a liveaboard chasing the best wave in the archipelago every single day. Wave count no land base can match; cabins, not villas; malaria belt and half-day medevac. Booking: Full-boat charters ex-Padang 9–12mo out.

The 4x4-guide model at its best: sand-bottom right points (Punta Conejo etc.) picked by wind/tide each morning, lineups effectively gated by access. World-class waves; thin beginner options. Booking: Camps 3–6mo; bring boards.

Boys-mode caveats (from the panel's defender). The family-lens gaps the defender flagged were closed in v6 — the universe now includes the boys-first rows (Mentawai boat charter, a North Shore Oahu base, G-Land, Zicatela-proper, Nias, Krui). Two reading notes remain: Nihi Sumba's rank is partly a luxury artifact (you'd be paying $$$$ for an infinity pool this mode says you don't need), and Taghazout's turnkey 9 encodes a learner-camp industry an advanced crew uses less of. Cost and min-days filter harder than the weights here: the top of this division skews $$$$ and 10+ days — Salina Cruz ($$) and Chicama ($) are the value line.

All 122 trips — solo / boys trip weighting

When to go where

The year splits cleanly in two: April–October belongs to the Southern Hemisphere swell machine, November–March to North Atlantic and North Pacific winter, with the Portugal/France shoulder peaking September–October. Gate-passing trips only.

Apr – Oct · southern season

The guarantee window

  1. Namotu / Tavarua island resorts 87.9 · Apr–Oct
  2. Telo Islands (Resort Latitude Zero) 87.8 · Apr–Oct

Three ways to book it

The boat-and-boards program

Mentawai, Telos, Banyaks, Namotu. A charter or island camp where the program IS the trip: dawn call, boat to whichever reef is firing, repeat. Maximum waves per day money can buy; book 6–12 months out.

The guided strike camp

Salina Cruz, Las Flores, Kavieng. A guide with a truck or panga and gated access to sand-bottom points. Near-private lineups without charter prices.

The mileage basecamp

Chicama, Popoyo, Cabo Ledo, Puerto Escondido. Cheap, consistent, uncrowded — park the crew for 10 days, surf three sessions a day, spend the savings on the next trip.

The top ten — strike division

The inversion of everything above: you don't book dates and hope — you watch the chart and fly when it's already confirmed. Consistency collapses to near-zero weight; what matters is strikeability — forecast visibility, T-minus-72-hour bookability, launch latency — plus wave ceiling and crowd. Gate: advanced score ≥ 7 and strike score ≥ 7. The trips the book-ahead divisions punish hardest (Rincón, Scorpion Bay, the Outer Banks, Skeleton Bay) are exactly what wins here.

Strike-mode caveats. This division assumes a crew that can drop everything on five days' notice — its scores price the trip, not your calendar. Hit rates are priors, not guarantees: a strike that whiffs still costs the flights (cheap for Rincón, painful for Skeleton Bay). And strikeability decays with fame — a forecastable spot everyone can see coming (Hossegor in September) arrives pre-crowded, which the crowd score already prices.

All 122 trips — strike mission weighting

Band = where the trip's rank lands when any one weight is perturbed ±25% — a tight band means the rank is robust. Go = this division's gate (advanced score ≥ 7 and strike score ≥ 7). When to go where

The year splits cleanly in two: April–October belongs to the Southern Hemisphere swell machine, November–March to North Atlantic and North Pacific winter, with the Portugal/France shoulder peaking September–October. Gate-passing trips only.

Apr – Oct · southern season

The guarantee window

  1. Soup Bowl (Barbados) — autumn strike 78.0 · Aug–Oct (hurricane swell)
  2. Chicama + Pacasmayo 76.8 · Apr–Sep
  3. Nova Scotia (Lawrencetown) 76.0 · Aug–Oct
  4. Outer Banks (Cape Hatteras) 75.8 · Aug–Oct
  5. Zicatela (Puerto Escondido proper) 75.7 · Apr–Sep
  6. El Zonte + El Tunco (La Libertad) 75.4 · Mar–Oct
Nov – Mar · northern winter

Winter season

  1. Rincón 78.9 · Nov–Mar
  2. Barbados (Freights + Soup Bowl) 77.6 · Nov–Mar
  3. Madeira (Jardim do Mar) 76.8 · Oct–Mar
  4. Fuerteventura 72.6 · Nov–Mar
  5. Famara (Lanzarote) 72.2 · Oct–Mar
  6. Taghazout + Tamraght 71.9 · Oct–Mar
Sep – Oct · shoulder

The sweet overlap

  1. São Miguel (Azores) 77.4 · Sep–Oct
  2. Peniche + Baleal 75.4 · Sep–Oct
  3. Ericeira 75.2 · Sep–Oct
  4. Bundoran + Sligo 75.0 · Sep–Oct

Three ways to book it

The drive-or-hop strike

Rincón, Outer Banks, Nova Scotia, Cocoa Beach. Watch the tropics; leave within 48 hours by car or a sub-5h nonstop. Cheap enough to whiff and try again next swell.

The five-day window

Azores, Peniche/Ericeira, Soup Bowl autumn, Zicatela. Groundswell visible ~5 days out, one nonstop plus a short transfer, walk-in lodging. The highest hit-rate class.

The unicorn hunt

Skeleton Bay, Scorpion Bay, Pavones. Waves that break a handful of days a year. Standing alerts, flexible tickets, and acceptance that some years the phone never rings.

No. 1 · 85.9

The top ten — strike division

The inversion of everything above: you don't book dates and hope — you watch the chart and fly when it's already confirmed. Consistency collapses to near-zero weight; what matters is strikeability — forecast visibility, T-minus-72-hour bookability, launch latency — plus wave ceiling and crowd. Gate: advanced score ≥ 7 and strike score ≥ 7. The trips the book-ahead divisions punish hardest (Rincón, Scorpion Bay, the Outer Banks, Skeleton Bay) are exactly what wins here.

85.9
USA (Texas)·Year-round·$$·min 3d·50–88°F · seasonal: trunks (May–Sep) to 4/3 (winter)·BOS→DFW/AUS + 1.5h drive ~8-9h

The flagship US pool: scheduled perfect waves, lifeguards, on-site casitas and a lazy river — a genuine resort, which is what qualifies it for the family division when pools are toggled on. Its score also remains the model's calibration diagnostic: it outscores every ocean trip. Booking: Book sessions online; private hire available.

Strike-mode caveats. This division assumes a crew that can drop everything on five days' notice — its scores price the trip, not your calendar. Hit rates are priors, not guarantees: a strike that whiffs still costs the flights (cheap for Rincón, painful for Skeleton Bay). And strikeability decays with fame — a forecastable spot everyone can see coming (Hossegor in September) arrives pre-crowded, which the crowd score already prices.

All 122 trips — strike mission weighting

Band = where the trip's rank lands when any one weight is perturbed ±25% — a tight band means the rank is robust. Go = this division's gate (advanced score ≥ 7 and strike score ≥ 7). When to go where

The year splits cleanly in two: April–October belongs to the Southern Hemisphere swell machine, November–March to North Atlantic and North Pacific winter, with the Portugal/France shoulder peaking September–October. Gate-passing trips only.

Apr – Oct · southern season

The guarantee window

  1. Soup Bowl (Barbados) — autumn strike 78.0 · Aug–Oct (hurricane swell)
  2. Chicama + Pacasmayo 76.8 · Apr–Sep
  3. Nova Scotia (Lawrencetown) 76.0 · Aug–Oct
  4. Outer Banks (Cape Hatteras) 75.8 · Aug–Oct
  5. Zicatela (Puerto Escondido proper) 75.7 · Apr–Sep
  6. El Zonte + El Tunco (La Libertad) 75.4 · Mar–Oct
Nov – Mar · northern winter

Winter season

  1. Rincón 78.9 · Nov–Mar
  2. Barbados (Freights + Soup Bowl) 77.6 · Nov–Mar
  3. Madeira (Jardim do Mar) 76.8 · Oct–Mar
  4. Fuerteventura 72.6 · Nov–Mar
  5. Famara (Lanzarote) 72.2 · Oct–Mar
  6. Taghazout + Tamraght 71.9 · Oct–Mar
Sep – Oct · shoulder

The sweet overlap

Three ways to book it

The drive-or-hop strike

Rincón, Outer Banks, Nova Scotia, Cocoa Beach. Watch the tropics; leave within 48 hours by car or a sub-5h nonstop. Cheap enough to whiff and try again next swell.

The five-day window

Azores, Peniche/Ericeira, Soup Bowl autumn, Zicatela. Groundswell visible ~5 days out, one nonstop plus a short transfer, walk-in lodging. The highest hit-rate class.

The unicorn hunt

Skeleton Bay, Scorpion Bay, Pavones. Waves that break a handful of days a year. Standing alerts, flexible tickets, and acceptance that some years the phone never rings.

Integrity checks

Checks run on the family weighting (the boys division reuses the same scores). A scoring model that just likes famous places is broken, so famous-but-flawed spots serve as null tests — and the weights get stress-tested rather than trusted.

  • Uluwatu ranks 98/122 and Noosa 111/122 despite world fame — crowds and (for Noosa) swell roulette cost them exactly as designed. Pass.
  • Sensitivity: the top 10 hold rank within ±2 places under every single-weight ±25% perturbation. Mid-table swings up to ±15 — treat those as a tier, not an ordering.
Adjudicated — Waikiki winter, rank 97. Earlier passes ranked it top-10 on a turnkey score of 9 — a beginner-only number smuggled in as a trip score — and on North Shore quality a mixed group can't ride (the base-pairing error caught in the v4 audit). Rescored as Waikiki-only; the null check now passes on its own.

Seven-persona panel review (v3)

  • The family weights survived: all seven persona vectors correlated 0.88–0.99 with the ranking, and six trips topped every vector — so the proposed reweight was rejected as redundant.
  • The structure didn't: five of seven seats flagged that an additive model lets consistency and crowd buy off a failing beginner score — hence the beginner floor instead of a weight.
  • Nine trips rescored on converging multi-seat evidence (Mentawai, Samoa, North Malé, Hacienda Iguana, Rote, others); cost stays out of the composite — budget is a filter, so it's a column. The family S-tier is, Las Flores excepted, also the $$$$-tier.

Adversarial coverage audit (v4)

  • The blind spot was property-level products — the list scored coastlines and missed resorts on validated corridors (Nihi Sumba, Rancho Santana, Mizata). 17 rows added; original 69 judged ~80–85% comprehensive.
  • The wave pools tell on the model: the best pool scores 91.6 under family weights — above every ocean trip — because "guaranteed, safe, zero-thought waves" literally describes a pool. With the toggle off they sit untiered as calibration rows; toggled on they compete, and in the family division only resort pools (Waco, Surf Ranch, The Wave Bristol) pass the gate.
  • Exclusions held: dozens of plausible destinations (Japan, Taiwan, Eleuthera, Tobago, Australia's points, Réunion) confirmed to fail the brief — recorded so they aren't relitigated.
The Family Wave Index · methodology, dataset and scoring script in the surf-trip repo (METHODOLOGY.md · data/trips.json · score.py) · scores are early-2026 expert priors; verify advisories, seasons and operators before booking.
